evidence_quotes.agenda: Never asked — a complex multi-stop partial move (apartment, two storage-unit stops, tight parking-garage access) goes straight into logistics.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer described a genuinely difficult access constraint (a very narrow, multi-level parking garage entrance) and the rep engaged with real back-and-forth trying to work out a solution, but ultimately couldn't resolve it before the customer got frustrated.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Call ends before pricing — the move gets declined ('if that's the case then we won't be able to cater this') after the customer, increasingly frustrated, asks to speak to someone else and the rep continues explaining rather than escalating, and the customer hangs up.

top_strength: Stayed engaged and tried to work through a genuinely hard logistical puzzle (narrow parking garage access requiring a truck-to-truck item transfer) rather than dismissing it outright.
coaching_note: This is the one call in the batch worth a manual audio review: the customer explicitly asked to speak to someone else about the access issue ('I wanna talk to somebody who is doing the moving or someone'), and the rep kept explaining instead of escalating — that's likely what tipped a solvable-but-tricky logistics problem into a lost, frustrated caller who hung up.
